text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat could hold summit to wrap up Hebron pact.
- Israeli parliament approves Economic Arrangements law accompanying the 1997 budget.
- Swiss leader: Holocaust compensation plan is blackmail.
- Jerusalem bus station moves to temporary new home.
- Israel Corporation doubles its 12.45 percent stake in Israel Chemicals (ICL).
- Customers sued banks for total of 320 million shekels in 1996 -- a rise of 16 percent from 275 million shekels in 1995.
- Inaugural Amman-Haifa flight due on Monday.
- General Bank seeks capital expansion.
GLOBES
- Shoul Eisenberg sells Israel Corporation his holdings in Israel Chemicals for $128 million.
- Treasury weighs alternatives for raising 620 million shekels following rejection of lowering of half-point tax credit for working women.
- Tel Aviv Stock Exchange in 1996: Real drop of about nine percent.
HAARETZ

- Netanyahu and Arafat intend to meet today to initial agreement. Fear in security establishment that members of parliament and cabinet ministers opposed to the deal will arrive in Hebron to encourage provocations against the evacuation.
- Prime minister: I am incapable of passing anything in the Knesset with this coalition. Aides: The prime minister could consider a unity government.
- Israeli team in secret Paris talks on south Lebanon.
MAARIV
- The intention is to meet -- and to close deal.
- Finance Minister Dan Meridor proposes privatising public housing and reduce number of apartments by 60 percent.
- Summary of 1996 - dollar rose 4 percent against the shekel.
- Gallup poll shows Israelis, who ranked third in the world in optimism a year ago, now rank 41st.
- Labour party leader Shimon Peres selected by Maariv's "Style" magazine as the best-dressed Israeli; first lady Sara Netanyahu selected the worst.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- U.S. President Bill Clinton in message to Netanyahu: Your decision on Hebron courageous. Arafat and Netanyahu expected to meet today.
